definitions.explanation: A formal New Year's greeting meaning 'respectfully celebrating the new year.' Used primarily on New Year's cards ({年賀状|ねんがじょう}) and in formal written greetings. Literally: {謹|きん} (respectfully) + {賀|が} (celebrate) + {新年|しんねん} (new year).

examples.japanese: ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I wrote 'Happy New Year' on the New Year's card.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|い}り{口|ぐち}→入り口：02507_iriguchi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}」⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}ている→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: There's a 'Happy New Year' decoration at the entrance of the company.

examples.japanese: ⟦{目上|めうえ}→目上：03804_meue⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、「{謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}」⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧{四文字|よもじ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{賀詞|がし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{正式|せいしき}→正式：03376_seishiki⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: For New Year's cards to superiors, it is considered proper to use four-character greetings like 'Kinga Shinnen.'

notes:
USAGE:
This is the most common formal four-character New Year's greeting ({賀詞|がし}). It is primarily written, not spoken. Appears on ⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧ (New Year's postcards), store decorations, and company greetings.

REGISTER:
Four-character greetings like {謹賀新年|きんがしんねん} and {恭賀新年|きょうがしんねん} are appropriate for superiors and formal contexts. Two-character greetings like ⟦{賀正|がしょう}→賀正：14993_gashou⟧ and ⟦{迎春|げいしゅん}→迎春：14994_geishun⟧ are considered less formal and should not be used toward superiors.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese New Year's cards (⟦{年賀状|ねんがじょう}→年賀状：06227_nengajou⟧) are sent to arrive on January 1st. The greeting printed on the card reflects the relationship between sender and recipient.
